source: SI, event-time holdout beyond MechDist and eculizumab case

sentences.waa_or: [With the same popularity term it reaches 1.10 (95% CI 1.10–1.11) per 1 SD, and its yearly interval lies below that of DisAtlas in each of the 22 decision years ([Supplementary Table @tbl:SI_event_time_or_yearly]).]
sentences.waa_2020: [Its yearly odds ratio is also lowest in 2020 (1.05, 95% CI 1.03–1.06), so the lower 2020 value is not specific to the learned representation.]
sentences.prereg_abs: [In diseases held out of benchmark tuning weighted Adamic–Adar places the next trialed disease at a median percentile of 31.0 (95% CI 30.2–32.0) among popularity- and connectivity-matched candidates, against 24.0 for DisAtlas, and at 33.8 (95% CI 32.9–34.7) against 24.7 among popularity-matched candidates.]
sentences.prereg_rule: [The pre-specified decision rule required the 95% interval of the DisAtlas advantage over weighted Adamic–Adar to lie above zero in both comparison sets and in both candidate pools, and all four comparisons met it ([Supplementary Table @tbl:SI_event_time_deltas]).]
sentences.prereg_adv: [Among diseases held out of benchmark tuning the advantage is 7.0 percentile points (95% CI 6.2–7.9) in the popularity- and connectivity-matched set and 9.1 (95% CI 8.3–10.1) in the popularity-matched set; among all diseases it is 3.6 (95% CI 3.0–4.2) and 8.5 (95% CI 7.8–9.2).]
sentences.prereg_years: [In the popularity- and connectivity-matched set the yearly interval lies above zero in 19 of the 25 decision years among diseases held out of benchmark tuning and below zero in none (other counts in Supplementary [](#sec:SI_et_subsets)).]
sentences.unmatched: [Without matching, disease popularity alone places the next trialed disease at a median percentile of 1.0 in diseases held out of benchmark tuning, against 4.5 for DisAtlas (Supplementary [](#sec:SI_et_comparison_sets)), which is why the two matched sets were the pre-registered co-primary analyses.]
sentences.auc_dropped: [It is computed exactly from the rank of the trialed disease among its matched candidates, with the drug's other new trials of that year left out of the candidates; the 9 new trials without any matched candidate are left out.]
sentences.auc_pooled: [Averaged over all 18,813 drug–decision-year pairs in diseases held out of benchmark tuning, the probability is 0.682 (95% CI 0.677–0.686) among popularity- and connectivity-matched and 0.680 (95% CI 0.676–0.685) among popularity-matched candidates, against 0.5 for random ranking ([Supplementary Table @tbl:SI_event_time_auc], yearly values in [Supplementary Table @tbl:SI_event_time_auc_yearly] and [Supplementary Figure @fig:SI_event_time_auc_methods]).]
sentences.auc_per_drug: [Averaging first within each drug, so that each of the 6,496 drugs counts once, gives 0.715 (95% CI 0.710–0.720) among popularity-matched candidates, which is higher because drugs newly trialed in only one decision year have higher probabilities (mean 0.738, 3,140 drugs) than drugs newly trialed in five or more decision years (mean 0.654, 1,131 drugs).]
sentences.auc_pop: [Within the matched sets popularity alone reaches 0.621 (popularity-matched) and 0.619 (popularity- and connectivity-matched), and on this scale shared-gene similarity is the closest reference score, at 0.647 against 0.682 for DisAtlas.]
sentences.e2_gene: [On the secondary endpoint, the share of drugs whose best-ranked new trial falls in the top 10%, shared-gene similarity is close to DisAtlas in diseases held out of benchmark tuning, with a difference whose interval includes zero, and slightly ahead among all diseases ([Supplementary Table @tbl:SI_event_time_deltas]).]
sentences.ms_proxy: [In every scored decision year from 1996 to 2006, 13 to 3 years before eculizumab's first trial in NMO spectrum disorder in 2009, multiple sclerosis ranked in the top 5.0–21.1% of held-out candidates for the drug.]
sentences.ecu_dating: [The event-time analysis records this pair in 2015 because its trial table does not contain the 2009 trial (NCT00904826); its earliest record of eculizumab in NMO spectrum disorder is an Orphanet entry for the phase 3 trial NCT01892345, which has no start date and is dated by its 2015 Orphanet validation.]
sentences.nmo_2007: [In decision year 2007, NMO ranks 45th of 1,728 candidates by DisAtlas and 121st by popularity alone, although NMO and PNH share no direct link in the graph on which the 2006 model was trained (3,455 diseases, 82,946 links) and are 2 steps apart.]
sentences.nmo_hops: [Restricting the candidates to diseases within 2 or 3 steps of PNH leaves the rank at 45 (top 4.3% of 1,058 and top 2.7% of 1,644), and among all 3,452 embedded diseases NMO ranks 86th (top 2.5%).]
